headline: The Pentagon is now giving defense contractors 21 days to come up with ways to dramatically accelerate weapons production as the Iran war continues to eat through U.S. stockpiles. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg directed industry to propose faster delivery schedules, increased production and investments in new manufacturing capacity. The scale of the depletion is significant. The Pentagon says the U.S. has expended more than 850 Tomahawks, 1,000 Patriot/THAAD interceptors and 1,300 tactical ballistic missiles in the early stages of the war. A CSIS estimate cited by the Washington Post puts global Patriot inventories at under 827, down from roughly 2,200 before the war, while THAAD inventories have fallen from 452 to fewer than 278. The Pentagon has announced framework agreements to expand production, including the recent effort to triple PAC-3 production and quadruple production of key THAAD components. But these agreements still require congressional funding.

headline: Iran's Supreme National Security Council has outlined six conditions it says must be met before the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened to commercial shipping: 1. Cease all threats and insults toward Iran. 2. Permanently end what Iran describes as its "war of aggression" against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Iraq, and Yemen. 3. Lift the naval blockade of Iran and withdraw all U.S. naval and air forces operating around the country. 4. Pay reparations for damage caused during the conflict. 5. Lift all sanctions imposed on Iran. 6. "Unconditionally" release all frozen Iranian assets. The demands underscore the significant gap that remains between the two sides. Several of the conditions, including ending the U.S. military presence in the region, lifting sanctions, and paying reparations, would represent major shifts in longstanding U.S. policy, making a near term resolution to the Strait of Hormuz crisis appear unlikely.

According to UKMTO, the fire has since been extinguished, all crew members and the vessel are safe, and no environmental pollution has been reported. The reported location closely matches an area where NASA's FIRMS satellite system detected a significant heat signature at approximately 1733 UTC yesterday, suggesting the two reports may be related. The incident occurred in a section of the Strait that has seen multiple recent attacks by Iran on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz using Omani waters.

headline: The Department of War has revoked former Secretary of the Air Force Frank Kendall's eligibility to access classified information and his ability to hold any sensitive Department of War position, citing an alleged "unauthorized disclosure of classified information regarding Air Force One's capabilities to a media outlet." Kendall served as Secretary of the Air Force from July 28, 2021, until January 20, 2025. While the Department of War has not identified the specific disclosure at issue, the action comes days after Kendall publicly commented on the capabilities of the VC-25B "Bridge" aircraft (the interim presidential aircraft converted from a Qatari-donated Boeing 747) during media reporting comparing it to the existing VC-25A fleet. Those reports highlighted that the Bridge aircraft lacks several capabilities of the legacy Air Force One fleet and will undergo additional upgrades. At this time, it remains unclear whether the revocation is directly related to those comments or to a separate alleged disclosure.
